first: Ha, a new face! I am Pell. I left years ago; the roads brought me back.
A basket, a trowel, some food. And I buy what you find, at a fair price. Mostly.
Herbs for me: I pay in coin, and a recipe too.
stranger: Baskets, trowels, food. I buy what you find.
They say bells ring in the deep ruins at night. Nobody has sold me one yet.
acquaintance: Herbs sell well. The best stand where the mist is thin at noon.
A glade lies west, past the old oak. The mist sits on it like a lid.
friend: Best customer this side of the river. Also the only one.
The garden behind the ruins was lovely once. Dark berries grew there, they say.

say: Sunleaf sells. I knew you had an eye. Or luck. Luck sells too.
Moonreed sells dear. A customer need not know what watched you pick it.
A stone idol. Some say old things like that sleep. Some say they wake.
Me, I say it sells. Keep it, or I pay fair for it. Mostly.
That bowl sold before I set it down. The hall keeps more, I would bet.

lines: Bells below the ruins? Travellers tell it three ways. All three, no charge.
One: the bells warn that the mist is coming. It takes what nobody looks after.
Two: something old is still awake down there. Who else lights the lanterns?
Three: someone buried old things on purpose. Leave them. Take what you need.
